transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me about your dream, however it comes back to you.
It was an old black and white film, grainy and flickering. I was in this big concrete car park at night, looking for my car.
a grainy old black and white car park at night. that already feels like it has its own hum to it.
Yeah, that hum is real. And I knew someone was following me, but every time I turned round there was only a thin grey dog sitting on the ramp, watching.
a thin grey dog, just sitting there, watching. not moving.
Right, just still. I started running up the stairs, and they kept going, floor after floor, but the same number painted on every wall — level 4, level 4, level 4.
level 4 every time. did you get the sense the stairs were actually taking you somewhere, or just keeping you moving?
Just keeping me moving, I think. I didn't feel like I was getting anywhere.
and the dog — was it still there on the ramp, or did it ever come up with you?
I don't remember seeing it while I was running. But when I finally came out on the roof, it was already sitting in my car — well, my car had turned into a little wooden rowing boat.
a wooden rowing boat on the roof. and the dog already in it, like it knew where you'd end up.
Exactly like it knew. It was parked between the lines, like a space meant for a car. And it was raining, but the rain was falling upwards, from the ground into the sky.
rain going the wrong way. how did that feel to be standing in?
It didn't really feel like rain, more like the air was moving wrong. I got in the boat with the dog, and the roof filled with water around us, and we floated. Then I woke up.
in the boat with the dog, floating as the roof filled. do you remember what the dog felt like being next to you?
No, I don't remember touching it or anything. It just sat there. It didn't feel comforting or threatening, just quiet.
just quiet, somewhere in between. and was anyone else ever in the car park, or was it only the two of you?
Only the two of us by the end. Before that, I only ever thought someone was following me, but I never saw anyone.
so it was the idea of someone, never a person. and then just you and the dog.
Yeah, exactly. The idea of someone. Then just the two of us in the boat.
how was that different, floating there with just the dog, compared to being chased in the stairwell?
It was calm. After all the running, the floating felt like everything just stopped. No more level 4.
all that running, and then it just lets you float. that's a strong ending.
It was a strong ending. I think that's why I remember it so clearly.
if you could pause the whole thing on one moment, the one that stays with you most, which would it be?
The moment I stepped out onto the roof and saw the dog already in the boat, with the rain going up.
that's the one. was there any object in that moment — the boat, the painted lines, anything — that felt like it mattered more than the rest?
The boat. It was wooden and small, but it still somehow fitted into the parking space between the lines. That felt important, though I don't know why.

so in this grainy black and white dream, you're in a big concrete car park at night looking for your car, and you know someone's following you, but every time you turn there's only a thin grey dog sitting on the ramp, still and watching. you run up the stairs and every floor says level 4, over and over, so it feels like you're not getting anywhere. when you finally come out on the roof, the dog is already sitting in your car, except your car has turned into a little wooden rowing boat, parked between the lines like it belongs there. the rain is falling upwards, from the ground into the sky, and the air feels wrong. you get in the boat with the dog, the roof fills with water, and you float. after all that running it goes calm and quiet, just you and the dog, and then you wake up.

did i get that right, or is there anything i missed?
You got it right. That's exactly how it was.
would you like to see it drawn?
Yes, I would. I'd like to see what you make of it.

there are a few ways it could be drawn. an old black and white film still: the world in grey, with a constant subtle flicker that makes stillness uneasy. a graphite pencil drawing: the image feels hand-drawn, with smudged grey tones that never quite resolve. a charcoal sketch: the image is bold and smudged, with deep black shadows and rough white highlights. or as the dream looked in real life: true colour, yet the scene is quietly off. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
The old black and white film still feels closest. The flicker was part of it.

ok, i'll start with the dog.

i picture them as thin, grey, short-haired, medium-sized. those are my guesses.

is anything different, or shall i leave it to you?
Your guesses fit. That's how it was. Leave it to you.

i'm sketching the thin grey dog and the concrete car park and the wooden rowing boat now, it'll appear on the right. only those for now, nothing else being drawn yet.

for the roof, i picture the open top of the car park, with parking spaces marked on the concrete. as guesses: it's night, but with the same harsh light as below, coming from lamps you can't see. everything in black and white. is anything different, or would you leave it to me?
Leave it to you. That all sounds right.

ok, then the rain.

i picture it as fine white lines rising from the ground, like the film's been reversed. is that right, or did it look different?
That's right. Fine, like the film's reversed. Everything else too.

sketching the roof of the car park now, it'll appear on the right. just that for now, nothing else being drawn.

i'll draw you too, since you're in it. would you like me to draw you as you are, or however i imagine you?
However you imagine me. I don't mind.
sketching everything now. it'll all appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks off once it's there, just say.
It looks right. Has the same grey, closed-in feeling. The only thing missing is the sense that I never see anyone, only the dog — but that's still there in the empty space.
the empty space carries it. no people, just the idea of someone.
That's exactly it. The idea of someone, but never a person.

the thin grey dog, the car park, the roof, the wooden boat, and you. all sketched now.

i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
The first one is right — the dog on the ramp, just watching. That's how it was.

that's the first moment then, the dog on the ramp just watching.

i'm drawing the next ones now, carrying on from there.
I hope they keep the same feeling. The running part had no end to it.
the running part had no end, that's right. the other moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right soon.
The stairs feel right too — the same number again and again. No sense of getting anywhere.

the stairs feeling endless was a big part of it.

the next moment is up on the right now — you turning around to look behind, but there's only the empty ramp. does that look the way you remember?
Yes, that's right. Empty ramp, no one there, just the feeling I wasn't alone.

the feeling of not being alone, even with no one there. that's exactly it.

the other moments are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right soon.
The third one is right too — the dog already in the boat, between the lines. That was the calmest part.

the boat moment was the calmest, i remember that too. that one's still coming though — right now the stairs are up, you running past the wall with level 4 on it. three of the six moments are on the right so far.

does that look the way you remember?
Yes, that's it. Level 4 on the wall, and the stairs going on. It looks like I'm not getting anywhere.
the endlessness of it is in there. i'm drawing the rest now, they'll keep appearing on the right.
The roof and the upward rain are right. The whole air felt wrong like that.

the air felt wrong, that was the whole point of the rain going up.

since that looks right, the last two moments will be drawn next, carrying on from the roof.
